SELECTED_INDEX: 5
CONFIDENCE: 0.55
EXPLANATION: The spectrum is dominated by aliphatic C–H stretches and bends (2969, 2897, 2837; 1453 cm⁻¹) consistent with a small saturated organic. The strong low-frequency features point to a heavy atom single bond: a prominent band near 670 cm⁻¹ and additional bands at 754 and 818 cm⁻¹ are compatible with C–Cl stretching modes in chlorinated ethanes, which typically show Raman-active C–Cl stretches/wags in the ~700–800 cm⁻¹ region and around ~500 cm⁻¹ (510 cm⁻¹ here) [cf. halogenated carbon rule analogs GFQ-046]. The presence of an ether group is supported by a C–O stretch near ~1007 cm⁻¹ and skeletal modes at 965/818 cm⁻¹, matching an alkyl ether bearing a chloro substituent. Together these features best fit COCCCl (candidate 5), while candidates with carbonyl (2) or sulfonyl (10) would be expected to show strong bands near ~1700 or ~1060/1300 cm⁻¹ not observed. GFQ-003 supports the C–H stretching/bending assignments.
